dimensions.assessment: Affects Medicare beneficiaries who purchase or rent ultralightweight manual wheelchairs with titanium or carbon fiber components, as well as suppliers.
dimensions.evidence: in the case where an individual purchases or rents from a supplier an ultralightweight manual wheelchair

dimensions.assessment: Clarifies billing rules and allows suppliers to charge beneficiaries the difference in cost for specific wheelchair materials.
dimensions.evidence: The supplier may charge the individual the difference between the supplier's actual charge

dimensions.assessment: Medicare payment amounts remain at existing levels, but out-of-pocket costs for specific material choices may shift to beneficiaries.
dimensions.evidence: payment to the supplier shall be made in the frequency and amount as would otherwise be made

dimensions.assessment: Amends Medicare Part B statutory provisions regarding HCPCS codes for a specific category of durable medical equipment.
dimensions.evidence: Section 1834(a) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395m(a)) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change taking effect on or after January 1, 2028.

missing_information: Exact count of affected Medicare beneficiaries
importance_detail.rationale: This bill requires CMS to establish specific HCPCS billing codes for ultralightweight manual wheelchairs with titanium or carbon fiber bases starting in 2028, allowing suppliers to bill beneficiaries for any price difference above standard Medicare payment.
